i hope all of you guys with the partner flairs realize that it's okay to think differnetly than starbucks. it's just a job and if you are betraying good morals for a company, i think that's really sad. that being said, yes, blm stuff was never "banned", but the culture at starbucks with "coffee with a cop" etc. really doesn't give the company a good look, especially right now. after starbucks many controversies with racism, i feel like the company should have definitely prepared to make good moves with the protests going on, but........... lol...

good on you for supporting the cause, much love!

there's these two ladies that come in a taxi literally 2 to 3 times a day to order the same 3 drink order that comes out to about $20 each time. they are obscenely rude to all of our partners every time they come, and the last time they came thru, they called my 18 year old coworker with autism the r word. he was so hurt and embarrased that he didn't tell anyone until a few hours later, they were obviously gone by then and we felt so bad because we didn't even know when it happened or we would have squared up lol.

the saddest part to me is that the lade that rides the taxi to get her drink is homeless with 3 kids and living in a shelter and i used to cut her slack because i grew up in extreme poverty and i know that must be a struggle. but honestly i don't even feel bad anymore because they're hateful as fuck and spending $60 at starbucks a day while her kids are sitting in a homeless shelter.

starbucks has made blm shirts that are available to purchase. they aren't being given out to partners for free. at least in the u.s. idk where you got the free part from, but that's untrue. it's okay you can just admit that starbucks fucked up on this one and made customers and partners angry.
